evidence: Cramer's V = 0.099 (negligible); a probe on centre alone reaches chance (lift +0.003). Center-1 supplies 537/641 patients, so there is little centre variation for a model to exploit.

mechanism: Acquisition site is encoded in the pixels
evidence: Centre is decodable from global image statistics with balanced accuracy up to 0.81 against a 0.167 chance floor (max lift +0.643). Still +0.476 after removing geometry, i.e. colour/exposure alone carry a site signature.
No probe on colour/exposure/geometry statistics beat chance by more than +0.102 for the lesion class. Whatever shortcut exists is spatial, not a global colour or exposure cue.
Training on a lesion-free crop — a region the annotation never touches, carrying no marker — retains 68%-95% of full-image balanced accuracy across all four modality/task combinations.

A black canvas showing only the white bounding rectangle retains 48%-189% of full-image performance. Lesion size and position are themselves strongly class-associated, so a detector is rewarded for box priors independent of appearance.

mechanism: Performance collapses on an unseen site
evidence: Training on Center-1 and testing on Centers 2-6 retains 52%-171% of internal balanced accuracy. External n is small (~100 patients) with a different class mix, so prevalence shift contributes alongside any site shortcut.

Splitting by image rather than patient raises balanced accuracy by +0.142 to +0.577, because 366 of 379 validation patients also appear in training. Not shortcut learning per se, but the largest single source of over-optimistic numbers on this dataset.
